notes: The ground this area owns (4,904 m2, 63 points): the ground round and under Blanton Hall that no other scripted area had, which the published tiles still drew as the 4 km context skirt (4,911 m2 of it inside, in three primitives) and the main model's WF_east_dorm_LiDAR_terrain_patch (560 m2). It is closed in on every side: webster's outline round the hall (its vertices 44 to 106, reused exactly: 1 m outside the walls on the south side and both ends) and the north-east area's edge (90, 455)-(176, 499), 5 to 11 m outside the north-west wall. No edge meets the far field or another model's ground, so every edge sample of edge_heights.json is dropped and the edge takes the neighbours' heights vertex for vertex (build_after). Blanton Hall (main model, the OpenStreetMap outline 313029108 extruded, walls down to 135.83 m, an entrance landing and door frames at the west end and the south door) stands inside and stays: the footprint runs under its walls, as the roadmap asked, so the old ground round it goes whole. Its ground floor has a passage at the west end in OpenStreetMap (footways 313029908 and 313029909, tunnel=yes) that the main model does not open. Main-model trees inside (five groups) stay; tools/evidence/trees.py finds no canopy peak of its own inside (bl_trees.json is empty). Evidence in /workspace/data/blanton: ortho2020 (x 40..240, y 370..540, 0.075 m), lidar.npz (same box, 0.5 m; the 2017 cloud only), osm.json (a copy of the webster area's fetch: Overpass did not answer on 2026-11-22). The building is not rebuilt here.
build_after_why: Along a shared edge the area built first sets the heights of the vertices both meshes have. Built by name this area would come before both neighbours and move their reviewed edge (webster's plaza and Lot 17, the north-east area's Webster Road and Stone Street apron) to its own heights; built after them it takes their edge as it is.
hold_neighbour_paving_why: The webster and north-east areas' paving along the edges they now share with this area keeps the bend their old edge samples (the skirt and the main model's terrain patch round the hall) gave it: sharing the edge drops those samples. Their soft ground lets go and follows the LiDAR, as this area's does.

supersede.notes: Patterns match 'mesh name material name' in the other sources' tiles. clip: their ground inside the footprint (triangle area with its centre inside, m2, from a dump of the published sw19 tiles): Context_skirt_3DEP_ortho_4km 4,912 (four primitives: the ortho strip tone twice and the litter tone twice), WF_east_dorm_LiDAR_terrain_patch 560; North_ground_ortho2020, MH_ground_ortho2020 and BD_farfield_3DEP 0, listed as in the neighbours so that any of their ground under the outline goes too. Not clipped: the hall's own entrance landing (TU_Blanton_entrance_0_landing, a walk material, 66 m2) and every part of the hall, and the main model's trees. drop: far_houses (none inside). overlap: every edge is shared (webster, north-east), so the cut reaches 0.6 m into both (supersede.OVERLAP) and no sliver of the skirt stands between the cuts.
